summary: Handle malformed backup manifests and exercise release verification tooling
details: Reject non-object paired-backup manifests before backup-file access and map JSON parser recursion errors to the existing controlled CLI failure result.
Add five bounded native Go fuzz entrypoints into actual Python release evidence, checksum, TAR/ZIP subject, offline signing-policy and paired-backup verification owners; register all 44 targets.

Use fixed synchronous workers with private scratch space, isolated credential-free environments, active assertions, input/output/time limits and real file hashes. Protect the worker protocol through the project fuzz-driver gate.
Retain the corrupt-GZIP regression and let bounded malformed streams reach the real verifier for rejection while preserving archive resource budgets.

Reuse one owned interpreter per foreground target to preserve the short mutation phase; rebuild private fixtures per request and retain every seed and assertion, with bounded synchronous requests and waited shutdown.

Run later minimization probes in a fresh bounded interpreter after the previous interpreter has stopped; preserve the original failed probe instead of misclassifying later inputs through a closed pipe.

Give the complete short campaign ten seconds per target so the observed cached audit-chain baseline leaves mutation time; retain every seed, single-worker execution and rejection of baseline-only runs.

compatibility.notes: Valid backup manifest and release evidence formats, generation commitments, publisher policy and signing/hash formats remain unchanged. Malformed backup JSON uses the documented error exit instead of an uncaught type/recursion exception. No repository setting, credential, tag or publication change.

security: Keep operator manifest and archive inputs structured and bounded. Context and verifier arguments are synthetic/offline consistency checks; no provider call, inherited credential, artifact execution or assurance upgrade occurs in a property.
limitations: Python internal coverage does not guide the Go mutation engine; bounded black-box properties are finite evidence, not exhaustive coverage.
Synthetic backup fingerprints do not prove database restoration. Historical public pins do not replace cryptographic signature verification or external publisher review.
